slice: Broad pre-code review of vocabulary, conversational copy, value language, trust boundaries, and cross-route continuity across Werkles.
sharedContext: Werkles must speak to ordinary people without requiring them to belong to a business or technology world.
The recurring defects are insider terms, Operator echo, robotic generated dialogue, homework tone, repeated disclaimers, unstable names, and buttons whose destination or consequence is unclear.

Approved product distinctions include: a person's private space is a Workshop; shared work between two or more Werklers becomes a Werkle; Public Bellows is the general library; Personal Bellows responds to the member's work; Crucible houses optional narrow checks; Match Deck compares possible collaborators.
Payment, identity, phone possession, funds evidence, and background screening remain separate facts and never become a universal trust score.
No member-facing copy change lands until actual review receipts are assimilated. No provider, schema, production, push, or deploy action is authorized.
liveStrings: One member journey. Different tools for different jobs.
knownGaps: The August 22 Ender, Bean, and Skybro copy packets have no terminal receipts and are not counted as active work.
Internal/provider language still appears on some member routes.
The same action or state may use different nouns across routes.
Generated conversations have improved but still require cross-route human re-walking.
The shared dirty worktree is not a clean release candidate.
